Rashi on Eruvin 51b:10:1.hebrew: שיש לו ב' בתים - אחד בזה ואחד בזה, והיה רוצה לילך לביתו שבעיר אחרת מע"ש ולשבות שם בשבת. ולא יצא מביתו אדעתא דקניית שביתה בסוף התחום ולחזור, אלא אדעתא למיזל עד התם, והחזירו חבירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:10:1.english: Where he has two houses - One in this [city] and one in that [city], and he wanted to go to his house in the other city on Shabbat eve and spend Shabbat there. And he did not leave his house with the intention of acquiring a Shabbat residence at the end of the [Shabbat] limit and returning, but rather with the intention to go all the way there, and his fellow turned him back.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:11:1.hebrew: איהו כיון דנפק לאורחא - משום הליכה ממש ולא משום לערב ברגליו, הוי ליה עני ויכול לומר: "שביתתי בסוף התחום", ויסיים מקום הניכר לו שם. ופלוגתא דאמוראי היא לקמן (שם): איכא למ"ד דאפילו לא אמר נמי, כיון דאנן סהדי דהתם בעי למיזל, כמאן דאמר דמי. וע"כ בדלא אמר מידי עסקינן: חדא, דלא קתני "ואמר שביתתי במקום פלוני"; ועוד, מדפליג ר"מ עלה ואמר "הרי זה חמר גמל", ש"מ בדלא אמר "שביתתי במקום פלוני" עסקינן, דהא ר"מ מודה בעני! וא"ת: ר"מ עשיר חשיב ליה להאי, דמשום דהחזיק בדרך פורתא לא משוי ליה עני — א"כ, דעשיר חשיב ליה ר"מ, "חמר גמל" אמאי? הא בביתו לא רצה לקנות, דהא אמר "שביתתי בסוף התחום", ושם לא יכול, דהא לאו עני הוא, ו"לא יזוז ממקומו" מיבעי ליה! אלא, בדלא אמר עסקינן, ור"מ נמי עני משויה ליה; ומשום דלא אמר כלום מספקא ליה: אי דעתו לקנות שביתה בסוף התחום, או שמא חזר בו לגמרי מלילך למחר לאותה העיר ודעתו לקנות שביתה בביתו; הלכך "חמר גמל" הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:11:1.english: Him, since he set out on his way - Because [he went out] for the sake of actual travel, and not [merely] to establish an eiruv with his feet, he has the status of a pauper, and he may say: "May my Shabbat residence be at the end of the [Shabbat] limit," and specify a place that is recognizable to him there. And this is a dispute of Amora'im below (there, 52a): There is one who says that even if he did not say [it] either, since it is evident to us that he wished to go there, it is considered as if he said [it]. And of necessity, we are dealing [here] with [a case where] he did not say anything [at all]: First, because [the Mishnah] does not teach: "and he said: May my Shabbat residence be in such-and-such place"; and furthermore, since Rabbi Meir disagrees with it and says, "Behold, this [person] is [in the status of] a donkey-driver [and] a camel-driver," conclude from this that we are dealing with [a case where] he did not say "May my Shabbat residence be in such-and-such place," for Rabbi Meir concedes in the case of a pauper! And if you say: Rabbi Meir considers this [person] a wealthy person, for merely because he set out on the road a bit does not make him a pauper — if so, that Rabbi Meir considers him a wealthy person, why is he [in the status of] a donkey-driver [and] a camel-driver? Behold, in his house he did not wish to acquire [residence], as he said: "May my Shabbat residence be at the end of the limit," and there he cannot [acquire residence], as he is not a pauper; so [the Mishnah] should have [taught]: "He may not move from his place"! Rather, we are dealing with [a case where] he did not say [anything], and Rabbi Meir also considers him a pauper; and because he did not say anything, it is uncertain to [Rabbi Meir] whether his intention was to acquire Shabbat residence at the end of the limit, or perhaps he changed his mind completely about going tomorrow to that city and his intention was to acquire Shabbat residence in his house. Therefore, he is [in the status of] a donkey-driver [and] a camel-driver.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:12:1.hebrew: הנך עשירים נינהו - ואפילו אמרו ״שביתתנו במקום פלוני״ אסור, דאי לא אמרו — פשיטא! אלמא כל ״במקום פלוני״, לר' יהודה: עני — אין, עשיר — לא. ולהכי נקט ״יש לו שני בתים״, דאי לא הוה ליה ביתא התם, לא הוה אמרינן ״כי לא אמר כמאן דאמר דמי״, דדלמא קא הדר ביה:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:12:1.english: These are wealthy people - And even if they said, “Our Shabbat residence [is] in such-and-such a place,” it is forbidden [for them to go]; for if they did not say [so], it is obvious! Apparently, regarding any [declaration of] “in such-and-such a place,” according to Rabbi Yehuda: [for] a pauper, yes; [for] a wealthy person, no. And this is why [Rav Huna] specified [that] “he has two houses”; for if he did not have a house there, we would not say [that] although he did not say [it], he is considered like one who said [it], because perhaps he had retracted [his intention].

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:13:1.hebrew: הלכה כרבי יהודה - וכרב נחמן, במקומי:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:13:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - And in accordance with Rav Naḥman, [who said that the dispute is] regarding [one who says: “My residence is] in my location.”

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:14:1.hebrew: הוה אתי מארטיבנא - רגיל דאתי בכל שבת מארטיבנא לפומבדיתא, והיה יושב ערב שבת בביתו ואומר: ״שביתתי בצינתא״ — מקום מסוים היה בין שני התחומין:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:14:1.english: He would come from Artibbena - [He was] in the habit of coming every Shabbat from Artibbena to Pumbedita, and he would sit in his home on the eve of Shabbat and say: “My [Shabbat] residence shall be in Tzinta” — a specific place that was between the two [Shabbat] limits.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:1.hebrew: עני הוא דאקילו רבנן גביה - הבא בדרך ואין עמו פת — הוא דאקילו רבנן גביה: לומר "שביתתי במקומי" כשאינו מכיר אילן או גדר, או למכיר — לומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני":
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:1.english: It is [only] a pauper that the Sages were lenient with him - One who is traveling on the road and does not have bread with him — it is regarding him that the Sages were lenient: to say, “My [Shabbat] residence is in my place” when he does not recognize a tree or a fence; or, for one who recognizes [a landmark], to say, “My [Shabbat] residence is in such-and-such a place.”

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:2.hebrew: אבל עשיר - כגון יושב בביתו, לא זו ולא זו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:1:2.english: However, a wealthy person - such as [one] sitting in his house, [is permitted] neither this nor that.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:2:1.hebrew: עיקר עירוב ברגל - ״שביתתי תחתי״, אפילו לעשיר, אם יצא והחשיך — זהו עיקר מצות עירוב. כדתני: ״לא אמרו לערב בפת כו'״, אלמא עיקר תקנת עירוב לר' יהודה ברגל היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:2:1.english: The primary [ordinance of] eiruv is by foot - [Declaring] "My resting place is beneath me" — even for a wealthy person, if he went out and darkness fell — this is the primary mitzvah of eiruv. As it is taught: "They only said to establish an eiruv with bread, etc." Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehuda, the primary enactment of eiruv is by foot.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:1.hebrew: זהו שאמרו חכמים - דמשמע דעיקר תקנתא לאו הכי הואי, אלא קולא בעלמא הוא שאמרו אצל העני לערב ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:1.english: This is what the Sages said - For [this phrasing] implies that the primary enactment was not this [way], but rather it is merely a leniency that they stated regarding a poor person, [allowing him] to establish an eiruv with his feet.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:2.hebrew: מאן קאמר ליה ר"מ - דאמר עיקר עירוב בפת:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:2.english: Who says it? Rabbi Meir - For he says [that] the primary [enactment of an] eiruv is with bread.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:3.hebrew: ואהיכא קאי אאינו מכיר או שאינו בקי בהלכה - ואמר ״שביתתי תחתי״, עלה קאמר ר"מ: ״וזהו שאמרו״. כלומר, דאפילו להאי דאמר ״במקומי״, קולא הוא דאקילו רבנן גביה, אבל לא זהו עיקר תקנת עירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:3.english: And to what is it referring? To: "He does not recognize, or is not well-versed in the halakha" - and said: "My Shabbat residence is beneath me" — regarding that [clause], Rabbi Meir said: "And this is what they said." That is to say, even for this one who says "[My Shabbat residence is] in my place," it is a leniency that the Rabbis granted him, but this is not the primary ordinance of an eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:4.hebrew: ולא אמרו לערב בפת - דמשמע דעיקר עירוב, כי איתקן — ברגל איתקן, ולא אמרו בפת אלא להקל על העשיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:3:4.english: And they did not say to establish an eiruv with bread - For [this] implies that the primary [enactment of] eiruv, when it was instituted, was instituted [to be established] on foot, and they said [to establish an eiruv] with bread only to be lenient for the wealthy person.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:4:1.hebrew: מחלוקת במקום פלוני - דאין כאן לא עירוב בפת ולא עירוב ברגל, אלא אמירה בעלמא — עלה קאמר ר"מ: עני — אין, עשיר — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:4:1.english: The dispute is [regarding] "in such-and-such place" - For here there is neither an eiruv with bread nor an eiruv by foot, but mere speech — regarding this, Rabbi Meir said: A pauper, yes; a wealthy person, no.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:4:2.english: However, “In my location,” everyone agrees, both a pauper and a wealthy person - For the primary [form of] eiruv is by foot:

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:1.hebrew: זהו שאמרו חכמים - דמשמע דעיקר תקנתא לאו הכי הואי, אלא קולא בעלמא הוא שאמרו אצל העני לערב ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:1.english: This is what the Sages said - Which implies that the primary enactment was not like this, but rather it is merely a leniency that they stated regarding a pauper, to establish an eiruv by foot.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:2.hebrew: אמי שבא בדרך וחשכה לו - והיה מכיר אילן ואמר: ״שביתתי בעיקרו״, דקתני: ״קנה שם שביתתו״, ועלה קאמר: ״זה הוא שאמרו: העני מערב ברגליו״, דהא קולא לעני הוא דאקיל, לא שיהא זה עיקר עירוב, אלא באומר: ״שביתתי במקומי״. ור' יהודה אמר: אפילו לעשיר שהיה יושב בביתו ואמר: ״שביתתי בסוף אלפים״ — הקילו נמי, ואף על גב דעיקר עירוב במקומי הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:2.english: On: "One who was coming along the way and it grew dark for him" - And he recognized a tree and said, "My resting place is at its base," where [the Mishnah] taught: "He has acquired a resting place there"; and regarding it, [the Mishnah] said: "This is what they said: A pauper establishes an eiruv with his feet" — for this is a leniency that was granted to a pauper, not that this is the primary form of an eiruv, but rather [the primary form is] when one says: "My resting place is in my place." And Rabbi Yehuda said: Even for a wealthy person who was sitting in his house and said, "My resting place is at the end of two thousand [cubits]," they were lenient as well, even though the primary form of an eiruv is [establishing it] in my place.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:3.hebrew: ולא אמרו - דמשמע: עיקר עירוב אינו בפת, אלא להקל על העשיר הוא דאיתקון — סתמא היא, וד"ה, ולאו מסקנא דמילתיה דר"י היא, דהא רבי מאיר נמי מודה בה, דעיקר עירוב ברגל במקומי:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:5:3.english: And they did not say - Which implies [that] the primary [enactment of] an eiruv is not with bread, but rather it was instituted to be lenient for the wealthy person — [this clause] is an anonymous [statement] and [the consensus of] all, and it is not the conclusion of the statement of Rabbi Yehuda; for Rabbi Meir also agrees with it, that the primary [enactment of] an eiruv is by foot [in the case of] "in my place."

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:1.hebrew: תניא כותיה דר"נ - דאמר מחלוקת במקומי, דאפילו היכא דאמר במקומי: לר' מאיר עשיר לא; ור' יהודה נמי לא שרי לעשיר אל במקומי, אבל במקום פלוני לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:1.english: It was taught [in a baraita] in accordance with Rav Naḥman - For he said [that] the dispute is [regarding one who says: "My residence is] in my location" — that even where he said "in my location," according to Rabbi Meir a wealthy person [may] not [establish an eiruv by foot]; and Rabbi Yehuda, too, did not permit [it] to a wealthy person except [when he says] "in my location," but in such-and-such a place, no.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:2.hebrew: ה"ג ולא יצא עשיר חוץ לתחום ויאמר תהא שביתתי במקומי - והאי חוץ לתחום לאו דוקא, אלא בסוף התחום. ואי דווקא חוץ לתחום — בתוך ד' אמות קאמר, שבו שביתתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:2.english: This is the correct reading: And a wealthy person may not go out beyond the Shabbat limit and say: "May my Shabbat residence be in my place" - And this [expression], "beyond the Shabbat limit," is not exact; rather, [it means] at the end of the Shabbat limit. And if "beyond the Shabbat limit" is exact — [the baraita] is speaking of [one who is] within the four cubits in which his Shabbat residence is.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:3.hebrew: שלא אמרו לערב ברגל - אפילו כי האי גוונא דאמר "במקומי", אלא למי שבא בדרך כו'. אלמא לר"מ, אפילו "במקומי": עני — אין, עשיר — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:3.english: That they did not say to establish an eiruv by foot - Even in a case like this, where he says "in my place," [it was permitted] only for one who was coming along the way, etc. Consequently, according to Rabbi Meir, even [when saying] "in my place": [for] a pauper, yes; [for] a wealthy person, no.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:4.english: And a wealthy person may go out beyond the [Shabbat] limit - If he wishes.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:5.hebrew: ויאמר שביתתי במקומי - אלמא, לר' יהודה לא שרי לעשיר אלא במקומי, כרב נחמן:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:6:5.english: And say: "My residence is in my place" - Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehuda, it is permitted for a wealthy person only [when he says] "in my place," in accordance with [the view of] Rav Naḥman.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:1.hebrew: א"ר יהודה מעשה באנשי בית ממל ובאנשי בית גוריון בארומא - מקום:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: An incident [occurred] involving the people of Beit Memel and the people of Beit Guryon in Aroma - [It is] a place.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:3.english: Raisins - Dried grapes that dried up and shriveled.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:4.hebrew: עניי כפר שיחין - סמוכין להן, לארומא, בתוך ד' אלפים:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:4.english: The paupers of Kefar Shiḥin - [They were] close to them, to Aroma, within four thousand [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:5.hebrew: ומחשיכין על התחום וכו' - אלמא עיקר עירוב ברגל, ובמקומי. ואע"ג דעניים היו, הואיל ובביתם איתנהו — כעשירים דמו, דא"א להם בלא מזון ב' סעודות, ואעפ"כ היו מערבין ברגלן ומחשיכין, דהיינו: במקומי, כרב נחמן. אלמא: עיקר עירוב ברגל, ומחשיכין על התחום. ואע"ג דלגבי עירוב עשירים הן — דהא מביתם יוצאין על כך, ויש להן פת — אפ"ה שרי, כי לית ליה שליח, לערב ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:8:5.english: And they would wait until nightfall at the limit, etc. - This demonstrates that the primary [form of] an eiruv is on foot and [by saying] "in my place." And even though they were paupers, since they were in their homes they are considered like wealthy people, for it is impossible that they do not have food for two meals, and nevertheless they would establish an eiruv by foot and wait until nightfall, which is [the equivalent of saying] "in my place," in accordance with Rav Naḥman. This demonstrates [that] the primary [form of] an eiruv is on foot, and waiting until nightfall at the limit; and even though regarding an eiruv they are [considered] wealthy — since they go out from their homes for this purpose and they have bread — even so, it is permitted, when one has no agent, to establish an eiruv by foot.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:1.hebrew: נמי דיקא - כרב נחמן, דלר' יהודה במקום פלוני עשיר לא, וכי פליג אדר"מ — במקומי הוא דפליג:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:1.english: [The Mishnah] is also precise - In accordance with Rav Naḥman, that according to Rabbi Yehuda, [with regard to] “in such-and-such place,” a wealthy person may not [establish an eiruv]; and when he disagrees with Rabbi Meir, it is [only regarding] “in my [present] location” that he disagrees.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:2.hebrew: מי שיצא - כל דהו, והחזיק בדרך לעיר שמערבין — שסמוכה לעירו לסוף ד' אלפים, ויכול אדם לילך מזו לזו ע"י עירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:2.english: One who set out - [Even] any amount, and took to the road toward a city for which an eiruv is established — which is close to his city at the end of four thousand [cubits], and a person can go from this [city] to that [one] by means of an eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:3.hebrew: והחזירו חבירו - דא"ל: עת חמה הוא, עת צינה הוא, כדלקמן (עירובין נב.):
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:3.english: And another person caused him to return - For he said to him: "It is a time of heat, it is a time of cold," as [stated] below (Eruvin 52a).

Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:4.hebrew: הוא מותר לילך - למחר לאותה עיר אחרת, וכל בני עירו אסורין:
Rashi on Eruvin 51b:9:4.english: He is permitted to go - On the morrow to that other city, and all the residents of his town are forbidden [to do so].

Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:3:1.hebrew: ואהיכא קאי אאינו מכיר - ולא בעי למימר דקאי א"מי שבא בדרך וחשכה לו", ודברי הכל — דמוכחא מתני' דבמאי דפליגי ר"מ ורבי יהודה איירי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:3:1.english: "And to which [clause] is it referring? To 'If he is not familiar'" - And [the Gemara] did not want to say that it refers to [the case of] "one who was coming along the way and it grew dark for him," and [that it is] the opinion of all, because the Mishnah proves that it is dealing with that which Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda dispute.

Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:5:1.hebrew: ולא אמרו לערב בפת אלא להקל מאן קתני לה דברי הכל - וא"ת: ולר' יהודה, מאי "להקל" איכא, כיון שאפילו בבית יכול לומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני"? וי"ל: דהאי "להקל" — היכא דליכא אילן או גדר ומקום מסויים במקום שרוצה לקנות שביתה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:5:1.english: "And they did not say to establish an eiruv with bread except to be lenient" — who taught it? Everyone - And if you say: According to Rabbi Yehuda, what leniency is there, given that even in [his] house he can say, "My [Shabbat] residence shall be in such-and-such a place"? And one can say: This "to be lenient" [applies] where there is no tree, or fence, or demarcated spot in the place where he wishes to acquire residence.

Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:7:1.hebrew: ויצא עשיר חוץ לתחום - קשה לר"י: דמדקרי ליה עשיר, דמשמע שרוצה לחזור וללון בביתו — ואיך יכול לחזור? והלא אין לו אלא אלפים מעירובו לצד עירו, ואפילו אם ביתו הוא הראשון בכניסתו לצד עירו, לא יהיה לו בתוך ביתו אלא ד' אמות; ואטו בשופטני עסקינן, שילון בביתו ולא יהיה לו אלא ד"א?! ונראה לר"י, דהא "חוץ לתחום" היינו חוץ לעיבורה של עיר; וכה"ג איכא בכיצד מעברין (לקמן עירובין דף ס.). ועוד אומר ר"י, דהאי דקאמר "ויצא עשיר חוץ לתחום" — לא שרוצה לקנות שביתה חוץ לתחום, אלא שרוצה לחזור ולקנות שביתה בתוך התחום; ונקט הכי משום רבי מאיר, דקתני "לא יצא עשיר חוץ לתחום", וקמ"ל: אע"פ דיצא חוץ לתחום ודמי השתא לבא בדרך, ואפ"ה אין יכול לערב ברגליו, דכיון דכל עיקר יציאה זו לא היה אלא כדי לערב; ואגב דנקט רבי מאיר, נקט נמי רבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 51b:7:1.english: "And a wealthy person will go out beyond the Shabbat limit" - This is difficult for the Ri: For since it calls him a "wealthy person," which implies that he wishes to return and lodge in his house — and how can he return? Behold, he has only two thousand [cubits] from his eiruv toward his city, and even if his house is the first [house] upon entering toward the side of his city, he will have within his house only four cubits! And are we dealing with fools, that he would lodge in his house and have only four cubits?! And it appears to the Ri that this "beyond the limit" means outside the city's outskirts; and there is a similar case in [the chapter] Keitzad Me'abrin (below, Eruvin 60a). And furthermore, the Ri says: That which it states, "And a wealthy person will go out beyond the Shabbat limit," does not mean that he wishes to acquire Shabbat residence beyond the limit; rather, [it means] that he wishes to return and acquire Shabbat residence within the limit. And [the baraita] formulated it this way on account of Rabbi Meir, who taught: "A wealthy person may not go out beyond the Shabbat limit," and [Rabbi Meir] teaches us: Even though he went out beyond the Shabbat limit and now resembles one coming along the way, nevertheless he cannot establish an eiruv by foot, because the entire primary purpose of this going out was solely in order to establish an eiruv. And since Rabbi Meir formulated [his statement this way], Rabbi Yehuda also formulated [his statement this way].
